steps.title: why the ladder still tries up to 10, but should not need to

args.text: The user asked directly why this scripts 10 numbered attempts when only 3 new catches are needed (party starts at 2, S03-39 wants 5). 10 was sized as pure headroom against two problems that are now fixed or greatly reduced: the ally-species engage-gap (fixed, operator_harness.gd::_find_entity) that used to eat several attempts before ever reaching a fight, and a shallow, guessed chip-down that left real catch odds far lower than catching.json's curve actually allows (fixed, chip_to_floor + throw_until_caught -- computed to each fight's own real floor, then thrown at until caught or out of tries). With those fixed, a real single-attempt sample landed a catch on the FIRST throw. Rather than guess a smaller number and risk under-provisioning on a bad RNG run, every numbered attempt's move_to_entity/interact_with pair now carries skip_if party_size>=5 (operator_harness.gd, added for this) -- once the team actually reaches five, every remaining attempt SKIPS in a few frames instead of walking, fighting and throwing for nothing. 10 stays as the ceiling for a genuinely unlucky run; it should rarely if ever be reached now.

steps.expected: RIG-17: matched on the prompt's own text (EncounterDirector, not the bramblebun, owns it) rather than entity relatedness, so this presses a real engage offer and refuses a fainted-ally message like "Ripplet is out of the fight"/"Put Moss away" instead of misfiring into it.

steps.title: trim it with quick attacks (do not kill it)
steps.expected: the target is WEAKENED as close to zero HP as this fight will safely bear -- not defeated, a defeated wild cannot be caught -- computed from the fight's own real per-hit damage rather than a guessed hit count or a guessed HP-fraction floor.
steps.observation: RIG, 2026-08-31: combat_quick x20 KILLED a 106 HP target, so a fixed times: 3 (S02's own proven opener) replaced it -- correctly avoiding a kill, but measured directly (gate-f-run-20260902T053310Z-s03enginefix) landing anywhere from 57% to 75% of max HP depending on the creature's own defence, the FLAT part of hp_factor's curve. A fixed enemy_hp_fraction 0.3 floor (this step's own immediately-prior version) fixed that but was still a guessed number, not a computed one -- called out directly by the owner in this session, 2026-09-02 ('if 5 presses took 70 health you could do another 2 without killing it. why wouldnt you? ... you can surely calculate what needs to be done'). chip_to_floor (operator_harness.gd, added for this) reads the live enemy hp before and after every swing and learns the actual per-hit damage this fight is dealing -- combat_math.gd::rolled_damage()'s only per-swing randomness against a fixed target is its +/-10% variance roll, so one real hit already bounds every later one -- and refuses the next swing only once the largest hit seen so far, scaled by safety_factor (1.25, past the 1.1/0.9=1.222 worst-case roll swing), would not survive. No fixed floor anywhere in this step; it chips exactly as far as the specific creature in front of it allows.

steps.title: aim and throw until caught, or out of tries (attempt 1)
steps.expected: the target is caught, or every allotted throw against it is spent -- a missed throw does not end the fight (catching.json's own cooldown exists so a failed catch can be re-thrown once the wobble clears; combat_manager.gd re-engages the same target on a miss), so this keeps throwing at the SAME chipped-down target instead of treating one orb as the whole attempt.
steps.observation: Owner directive, this session: "we should chip down then throw orbs til we catch." The ladder used to spend exactly one orb per numbered attempt (arm aim, track, throw once, wait) and then move on regardless of outcome -- discarding real, intended-to-be-retried catch chances the moment a single throw missed, even though nothing about the game ends the fight on a miss. throw_until_caught (operator_harness.gd, added for this) re-arms the aim, re-tracks the live target and throws again, up to max_throws times, stopping the instant the party actually grows.

steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6 modal-holds-locomotion audit, upgraded per FINDING-CAPSTONE3-S03-CATCH-LOOP-STALL-2026-09-01. steps.title: cycle to a live party member before attempt 2 (T2-BUILDPLACE)
steps.expected: REORDERED after a 3-attempt verification chain (ralph/reports/gate-f-run-20260901T220548Z-s03fix). Revive-then-cycle, not cycle-then-revive: when BOTH party members are fainted at once (attempt-b's own fight fainted the second member here), cycle_active() run FIRST has no live member to switch to and is a no-op, and a revive run afterward heals a creature without ever making it the ACTIVE one -- encounter_director.gd's `_ally` pointer stays on whichever (still-fainted) creature was active when the block started, so interaction_offer()'s priority-100 lockout persists even though someone in the roster is healthy again. Reviving FIRST, then cycling, means cycle_active() has a genuinely live member to find by the time it runs. autoload/party.gd::cycle_active() remains a documented no-op when the active creature is already the only healthy one, so this is still safe to run unconditionally.

This file was transcribed against a version of the chapter that no longer ships, and most of what GAME-F5 recorded against the gathering economy was this file asking for the wrong building. FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD changed three shipped numbers and none of them reached here. (1) data/config/tournament.json entry.min_party_size is 5, not 3 -- and it was already 5 on candidate 453107fb, the very SHA the audit measured, so DEFECTS.md's 'tournament.json requires min_party_size: 3' was wrong about its own candidate. data/progression/objectives.json's tournament_build_team says it in words: 'Build your full team of five for the village tournament.' (2) data/config/progression.json home.required_pieces is {camp: 1, creature_bed: 1} -- ONE camp and ONE bed. This file built camp+floor+wall+door+roof and THREE beds and measured the village's gathering budget against that: 45 wood / 17 stone / 34 fiber, against a real requirement of 18 / 8 / 18 that the twenty village nodes (28 / 9 / 32 in one pass) cover with room to spare. (3) The bed rung's flag is creature_bed_built, not creature_bed_built_3; objectives.json calls one bed 'the mandatory care lesson' and tests/test_quest_log.gd asserts the rung 'must not require one bed per tournament entrant'. The floor/wall/door/roof and second/third bed blocks are removed rather than retained-and-skipped: a step that builds something the game does not ask for is not extra coverage, it is a false economy measurement, and that is exactly what GAME-F5 reported.
